scholarships.title: MOE Elite Scholarship Program for Lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African Countries
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Education (MOE), Republic of China (Taiwan)

existing.description: The MOE Elite Scholarship Program was created by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) under its New Southbound Policy to encourage university lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African countries to pursue graduate degrees in Taiwan, with priority given to doctoral study. Awardees receive a total monthly award of NT$25,000 for up to two years of a master's programme or three years of a doctorate, reviewed annually; participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total and pay the remainder to the student as a monthly stipend, which at Taipei Tech works out at around NT$14,000 per month in years one to three and NT$12,000 in year four. Applicants must currently hold a lecturer or more senior post at a university in an eligible country with that position on hold, must supply an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate, and apply through the participating university, which submits the case for MOE review. Around 100 places are awarded per academic year across a three-year cycle.
eligibility: Must be a university lecturer, assistant professor or professor currently employed at a public or private higher education institution in an eligible country.

Eligible Southeast and South Asian countries: Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bhutan.

African route: applicants from any African country who are either current university lecturers or professors with an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English, or have at least three years of university researcher experience in an African country with research publications or papers.
Must be a citizen of the country where they hold the teaching position.
The teaching position must be on hold because of the studies.
Must provide an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English; the African researcher route requires an employment certificate in English plus research publications.
Must not hold Taiwan (R.O.C.) nationality or overseas Chinese student status.

Must not be enrolled in, or hold a retained admission at, a university in Taiwan. This restriction does not apply to a student on course to graduate who is pursuing a next degree, provided they are still a lecturer from a South or Southeast Asian country.
Must not previously have studied in Taiwan for a degree at the same level.
Must not be an exchange or dual-degree student under a partnership agreement with an overseas institution.
Must not have received stipends through this programme for more than three years.
Must not be a recipient of any other scholarship or financial assistance from a Taiwan government agency or a foreign government.
Must satisfy the participating university's own admission and English-taught programme requirements.
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens and current university lecturers (or assistant professors and professors) at a public or private higher education institution in an eligible South or Southeast Asian country, or lecturers meeting the African route, whose teaching position is on hold because of their studies. Applicants must hold an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English and must not already be enrolled in, or hold a retained place at, a Taiwanese university, have studied in Taiwan at the same level, hold another government scholarship, or be an exchange or dual-degree student.
benefits: NT$25,000 per month total award from MOE, of which tuition and credit fees are deducted first.
Full tuition fee subsidy out of the award; Taipei Tech states tuition and fees are subsidised for up to 4 years.

Post-tuition monthly stipend. At Taipei Tech this works out at around NT$14,000 per month in years 1 to 3 and NT$12,000 per month in year 4, because the full tuition is deducted from the total MOE award.
Annual review, with enrolment procedures to be completed every semester to keep the scholarship continuous.
coverage: Total monthly award of NT$25,000 from MOE.
Tuition and credit fees are paid out of that total award, after which the remaining balance is paid to the student as a monthly stipend.
Stipends may be used for tuition and miscellaneous fees, thesis supervision, insurance, accommodation, internet use and living allowance.
Remaining stipends may not be retained or deferred.
requirements: Hold a current university lecturer, assistant professor or professor post at an institution in an eligible country.
Provide an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English.
Have the teaching position on hold because of the studies.
Apply to a participating university and, where required, choose a full English-taught programme.
Submit the MOE-Elite form and documents by the deadline stated in the university's post-admission email.
Complete enrolment procedures every semester to keep the two or three-year scholarship continuous.
Apply for renewal each year, subject to review.
documents: Up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English (mandatory for lecturers)
For the African researcher route: Employment Certificate in English plus research publications
The MOE-Elite online application form, completed via the link emailed by the university's Office of International Affairs
Regular university registration and tuition payment documents
existing.english_requirement: Not an English-language test requirement. The scholarship supports study in full English-taught programmes, and participating universities require applicants to choose a full English-taught programme where applicable, with courses taught in English rather than merely enough English courses to meet credit requirements.
application_method: Apply for admission to the participating university, choosing a full English-taught programme where required, and indicate the scholarship track in the admission application where the university provides one.
After admission results are announced, the university's Office of International Affairs emails the MOE-Elite guidelines, forms and upload links to eligible admitted students.
Complete the online application form via the emailed link and upload the Lecturer Certificate and all other required documents before the deadline stated in the email.
Complete regular university registration and tuition payment during the tuition payment period.
MOE reviews all applications and announces recipients; the university notifies selected students and shares the stipend plan.
Confirm the six-month stipend plan by email, after which the stipend is disbursed monthly.
existing.selection_notes: The programme is administered under the MOE Elite Scholarship Program Action Plan and was created in accordance with the New Southbound Policy Work Plan announced by the Executive Yuan in December 2016, under the MOE New Southbound Policy Talent Development Program. Priority is given to doctoral programmes. The university evaluates the admission application by department, and the MOE then reviews and determines the scholarship award. Published quota: one hundred students per academic year over three academic years, for a total of three hundred students. MOE allocates the quota, so entry is limited to new PhD students in the relevant intakes and can involve a waitlist.
existing.best_fit: University lecturers, assistant professors and professors from South and Southeast Asian or African countries who have secured an offer from a participating Taiwanese university, whose institution can place their post on hold, and who hold an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate.
existing.notes: Critical money nuance: NT$25,000 per month is the TOTAL award, not the amount in the student's pocket. Participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total first and split only the remainder into a monthly stipend. Taipei Tech publishes the resulting figures as around NT$14,000 per month in years 1 to 3 and NT$12,000 per month in year 4. Applicants should not budget on NT$25,000 of disposable income. Duration also varies by university: the standard MOE terms are 2 years for a master's and 3 years for a doctorate with annual review, while Taipei Tech runs the award for up to 4 years and restricts it to newly admitted PhD students. The scheme is quota-limited at 100 places per academic year, and waitlisted candidates approved by MOE must repay any previously disbursed stipends. Do not confuse this with MOE's Taiwan Scholarship Program, which pays tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NT$40,000 per semester plus a monthly living allowance of NT$15,000 or NT$20,000.
existing.duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme and up to 3 years for a doctoral programme under the standard MOE terms, reviewed annually. Some participating universities extend this, and Taipei Tech runs the award for up to 4 years.
existing.application_period: Tied to each participating university's admission cycle, with published Fall application windows running from around mid-December to mid-March, followed by a post-admission document submission stage with its own email-stated deadline. MOE announces recipient lists around late October for Fall and late April for the African Spring intake. The AY2026/27 Fall window closed in mid-March 2026; the next is expected to open around mid-December 2026 for 2027 Fall entry.
existing.deadline_display: There is no single ministry deadline. Applicants apply through the participating university's admission application, and the published application windows have been mid-December to mid-March for Fall entry (National Cheng Kung University's AY2026/27 window was mid-December 2025 to mid-March 2026). After admission results, the university emails the MOE-Elite guidelines, forms and upload links, and applicants must submit by the deadline stated in that email. MOE then announces recipients, around late October for Fall intake and late April for the African Spring intake.
existing.program_type: Government graduate scholarship for university lecturers from South, Southeast Asia and Africa to study in Taiwan (Ministry of Education, New Southbound Policy talent development)

scholarships.title: MOE Short Term Research Award (STRA)
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan)

eligibility: Be a PhD student at an overseas government approved and registered public or private university or tertiary college, or be a postdoctoral research fellow now undertaking research at an overseas institution
Not hold an R.O.C. (Taiwanese) passport
Not be currently visiting, residing, studying, interning, teaching or researching in Taiwan
Not be receiving other financial assistance from a Taiwanese government agency or educational institution for a research project
Not be an exchange student under a Taiwan-overseas academic cooperation agreement during the proposed research period
Not have received an STRA award within the last 5 years
Exclude scholars from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao
existing.eligibility_summary: Overseas PhD students and postdoctoral researchers who do not hold an R.O.C. passport, are not currently in Taiwan, hold no other Taiwanese government or institutional research funding, are not exchange students, and have not received an STRA in the last 5 years. Scholars from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao are excluded.
benefits: Economy class return airfare to Taiwan
coverage: Monthly research allowance of NTD 25,000 for PhD students and NTD 40,000 for postdoctoral fellows
Economy class round-trip airfare on the most direct route between the applicant's place of residence and Taiwan
requirements: Research topic related to Taiwan in a humanities discipline, the social sciences, a culture and/or arts field and/or related comparative research
Application submitted to a host institution in Taiwan
Research stay of between 2 and 6 months
application_method: Identify a host institution in Taiwan (a university, tertiary college or a research organization affiliated with the MOE, such as the Center for Chinese Studies or the National Academy for Educational Research)
Submit the application to that host institution so that it arrives by 30 September
existing.selection_notes: The host institution receives and processes the application under the Directions Governing Ministry of Education Subsidies for Short Term Research Awards.
existing.best_fit: Overseas PhD students and postdoctoral researchers whose proposed research topic relates to Taiwan and who can host the research at a Taiwanese institution.
existing.notes: This is a research stay award, not a degree scholarship; the published monthly amount differs by career stage.
existing.duration: Between 2 and 6 months of research in Taiwan
existing.application_period: Annual; applications submitted by 30 September for research the following year
existing.deadline_display: Applications for research in Taiwan in the following year must arrive at the host institution no later than September 30 each year
